question.text: Per IND-AS 113 and the IPEV Valuation Guidelines, 'Fair Value' of an AIF portfolio investment is best described as:

answer.text: The historical cost of acquisition adjusted for inflation
The highest bid received in a competitive auction
The price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date
The weighted average of DCF, multiples and asset-based valuations

explanation.text: The Logic: IND-AS 113 defines Fair Value exactly as in option C — the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. The IPEV Guidelines adopt this definition as the central theme for valuing private equity portfolio investments. The Trap: Historical cost adjusted for inflation is a book-value concept, not fair value. 'Highest bid' captures only one side of a transaction and is not the orderly-transaction price. A weighted average of methods is a manager-chosen triangulation technique, not the IND-AS definition itself. Note: The 'orderly transaction' qualifier is integral — a distressed or forced-sale price is not fair value under IND-AS 113 or IPEV.
